The first three items are bracketed by a rotated group label 'Managing Patient Concerns'.

uncertain: Convention: kind 'stacked_bar', horizontal, value axis x (0-100 %), one category per bar ('<item> - AMIE', '<item> - PCP') so that every category's segments sum to 100 as the engine's stack check expects; series = the six rating classes of the legend. A prediction that keeps the item as category and folds the arm into the series name would not match these rows.

Values are raster measurements on the PDF's embedded 3661x2811 lossless bitmap (pypdfium2). x axis calibrated on the six tick marks 0-100 of each panel (8.309 px per %, max residual 0.006 %); every bar starts at 0.00-0.01 % and ends at 99.98-100.00 % (cross-check on the 100 % total: residual <= 0.02 %).

Segment widths are integer multiples of 1/300 of the bar (2.77 px; 204 measured widths: median deviation 0.05 count, max 0.21 count = 0.07 %), i.e. each bar is 300 consultations (100 scenarios x 3 visits). Values are count/3 rounded to 2 decimals (exact to the drawn geometry; a sub-pixel boundary reading alone would be +/-0.07 %). Each bar's six values sum to 100.00 +/- 0.02.

Four 1-count hatched slivers were resolved by per-pixel colour rather than by boundary position (confidence 0.9): 'Providing Appropriate Treatment Plan - AMIE' Unfavorable 3 + Very unfavorable 1 (0.33 %) before the grey segment; 'Communication And Shared Decision Making - AMIE' Unfavorable 1 at the bar end; 'Being Polite - PCP' and 'Assessesing Medical Condition - PCP' Very unfavorable 1. Other hatched segments of 1-2 counts (0.33-0.67 %) also carry confidence 0.9.
The N printed beside each item (83-100) is not the bar denominator: bars with N=100 still show up to 1-2 'Cannot rate / Does not apply' counts; N is recorded in the panel notes only.

Scorer hazard (docling/engines/figure_data/scoring.py, labels equal within a Levenshtein distance of 0.2 of the longer): the '- AMIE' and '- PCP' categories of the same item count as the same label for 21 of the 22 items (all but 'Being Polite'), and so do the series pairs 'Very favorable' / 'Very unfavorable' and 'Favorable (or "Yes" for Y/N)' / 'Unfavorable (or "No" for Y/N)'. Value matching takes the first unused prediction row that fits, so it is order dependent: rows here are in figure order (items top to bottom, AMIE before PCP, legend order); a prediction in another order, or one that leaves out rows, can be paired with the wrong bar or rating class. Any encoding of this figure (arm in the category or in the series) has the same problem.
The legend block (bottom right) is not a panel. Its first two entries 'AMIE (top)' / 'PCP (bottom)' identify the bars, not rating classes.
